chunks: And Ḥanān ibn Sudayr narrated from his father, who said:
I asked him about fasting on the Day of ʿArafah, and I said: “May I be your ransom, they claim that it equals the fasting of a year.”
He said: “My father, peace be upon him, would not fast it.”
I said: “And why, may I be your ransom?”

He said: “The Day of ʿArafah is a day of du'a and asking, so I fear that it may weaken me from du'a, and I dislike fasting it, and I fear that the Day of ʿArafah may be the Day of al-Aḍḥā, and that is not a day of fasting.”

key_terms.مَسْأَلَةٍ: asking and beseeching Allah for one’s needs
key_terms.يُضْعِفَنِي: make me weak or diminish my strength

ai.seo_question: Should one fast on the Day of ʿArafah, or is it better to devote the day to du'a?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses fasting on the Day of ʿArafah and presents the Imam’s preference not to fast it. The reason given is that it is a day especially devoted to du'a and beseeching Allah, and fasting may weaken one from that worship; there is also concern about mistakenly fasting on the day of Eid al-Aḍḥā, when fasting is not permitted.
